target: Reject symbolic-link state-lock sidecars before acquisition, and on Unix open the lock with O_NOFOLLOW, so an atomic state rename cannot migrate subsequent acquisitions from the locked old inode to a new state inode.

baseline_observations.case: Pre-create <state>.lock as a relative symlink to state.json; hold the first CLI at a FIFO report write after its atomic state save, then run a second consuming CLI while the first remains alive.
baseline_observations.first_process: Still alive and blocked on FIFO after replacing state; its lock file descriptor refers to the pre-rename state inode.
baseline_observations.second_process: Exit 0; acquired through the same lock symlink after state rename, consumed exec/sum and wrote its own report.
baseline_observations.state_transition: pending directives 6 -> 5; consumed tombstones 0 -> 1 while the first lock holder remained alive.

criteria.pass: A pre-existing final or dangling lock symlink is rejected before polling, consumption, state mutation or report output; the error is explicit and no lock target is followed.

The real old two-process FIFO scenario permits the second consumer while the first is alive, while the new first process exits nonzero before changing the initial state; all sentinel files and the symlink remain unchanged.
Regular lock files retain exclusion before and after save_atomic, and a pre-existing hard-link sidecar does not migrate to the replacement state inode.
Unix lock acquisition uses O_NOFOLLOW in addition to the portable symlink precheck; other open and lock errors remain explicit and fail closed.

An independent Python oracle reconstructs process and filesystem transitions, checks liveness, FIFO evidence, state schema and hashes, and passes known-answer self-tests plus synthetic fake-report rejection before accepting real old/new reports.
Normal state/report controls remain byte-identical where applicable; existing wave, execution, replay, output-path and atomic-write anchors do not drift, and the complete Rust/Python gate passes.
A no-.git archive of the implementation commit with an initially absent CARGO_TARGET_DIR rebuilds successfully, and that clean new binary generates the final real-process differential.

development_corrections: The first fixture assumed a snapshot field named pending; actual v4 uses directives. It stopped during setup before the attack processes ran.

The second fixture printed the successful exploit but its final assertion incorrectly expected six directives after consuming one instead of five; the assertion was corrected and the entire scenario rerun to exit 0 before CONFIRMED was recorded.
not_proven: Rejecting symbolic-link sidecars does not prevent a hostile actor from replacing a regular lock pathname after acquisition, nor does it constrain non-cooperating writers or a hostile OS.
No distributed lock, cross-host semantics, CAS, WAL, fsync, crash-power-loss durability or post-create ledger-temporary race defense is added.
The portable precheck alone is not claimed to eliminate non-Unix check/open races; Unix uses O_NOFOLLOW for the actual open.
No publisher authentication, federation activation, external QF-OS/QIOS compatibility, formal execution proof or zero-knowledge proof is claimed.
